City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, September 5, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Harrington
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. NATIONAL HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH

  B. INTRODUCTION OF NEW POLICE CHIEF EDWARD ELIZALDE

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of August 15, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are
  presented to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. ORDINANCE NO. 691 RELATING TO ELECTRONIC AND PAPERLESS FILING
  OF FAIR POLITICAL PRACTICES COMMISSION (FPPC) CAMPAIGN
  DISCLOSURE STATEMENTS AND STATEMENTS OF ECONOMIC INTERESTS
  – SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 691 was introduced and the first reading was conducted by
  title only by a vote of 4-0 vote of the City Council at the August 15, 2023, City
  Council meeting. Ordinance No. 691 would require electronic filing of
  campaign finance statements and Statements of Economic Interests. The cost
  to add electronic filing of campaign finance statements is $1900 annually.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive full reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 691 adding Chapter 40 “Electronic and Paperless Filing of Fair
  Political Practices Commission Campaign Disclosure Statements and
  Statement of Economic Interests” to Title III “Administration” of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code.

  D. HOME PRESERVATION PROGRAM CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT WITH
  SAN GABRIEL VALLEY HABITAT FOR HUMANITY FOR THE HAYES HOUSE
  REPAIRS

  The City of San Gabriel owns the property located at 546 West Broadway,
  which is the site of the Hayes House, San Gabriel Historical Museum, and Jail,
  is operated and maintained by the San Gabriel Historical Association (SGHA).
  The structures are in need of maintenance and repairs. In July 2023, the San
  Gabriel Valley Habitat for Humanity informed the City that they will be
  assisting SGHA with some of the repair items. The amount of the contract is
  $7,100. These funds are part of the Fiscal Year 2023-24 adopted general fund
  budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Home Preservation Program Construction Contract with the
  San Gabriel Valley Habitat for Humanity for repair work to the Hayes
  House; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the Home Preservation Program
  Construction Contract.

  E. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-10 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $37,900 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY TO MEDINA BRAVO
  CONSTRUCTION,  INCORPORATED  FOR  THE  REMOVAL  AND
  REPLACEMENT OF SEVERAL SECTIONS OF CONCRETE SIDEWALKS
  ALONG THE 100 AND 200 BLOCKS OF GERONA AVENUE

  The 100 and 200 blocks of Gerona Avenue are residential streets lined with
  Camphor Trees on both sides of the street, creating a large canopy over the
  middle of the street. It is an aesthetic and popular street because of the
  canopy’s tunnel-like feel driving through it. The Camphor Tree is a large
  species of tree with an aggressive shallow root system. Several sections of
  sidewalks have been displaced or cracked and need to be repaired. The total
  cost for this project is $37,900, plus a 10% contingency.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Categorically
  exempt per Section 15303 of the State CEQA guidelines regarding New
  Construction or conversion of small structures.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council award a contract to Medina Bravo
  Construction, Incorporated as the lowest responsive and responsible bidder,
  authorize the City Manager to execute Contract No. 23-10 for $37,900 and
  approve a Purchase Order with Medina Bravo Construction, Inc. in an amount
  not to exceed $41,690 which includes a 10% contingency using the Gas Tax
  account 122-800-41-96-609.

  F. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-11 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $32,000 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY TO MEDINA BRAVO
  CONSTRUCTION, INCORPORATED FOR THE INSTALLATION OF EIGHT
  NEW RAMPS AT TWO CITY INTERSECTIONS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023  4
   The Field Operations Division within the Public Works Department is
  responsible for the maintenance of all sidewalks and Americans with
  Disabilities Act (ADA) ramps at City Intersections. ADA ramps provide a
  smooth and safe path of travel from the sidewalk to the street for people with
  disabilities. Due to recent staffing shortages, and a growing backlog of
  sidewalk maintenance requests, staff is seeking assistance from outside
  contractors for the installation of ADA ramps. The total cost for the project is
  $32,000, plus a 10% contingency.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Categorically
  exempt per Section 15303 of the state CEQA guideline regarding New
  Construction or conversion of small structures.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute Contract No. 23-11 for $32,000;
  and
  2. Approve a Purchase Order with Medina Bravo Construction, Incorporated
  in an amount Not to exceed $32,000 which includes 10% contingency
  using the Transportation Development Act Article 3 fund account 122-
  800-44-96-604.

  G. MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES GATEWAY
  REGION INTEGRATED REGIONAL WATER MANAGEMENT JOINT POWERS
  AUTHORITY FOR ANNUAL COST SHARING FOR MONITORING
  PURSUANT TO THE HARBOR TOXIC POLLUTANTS TOXIC POLLUTANT
  TOTAL MAXIMUM DAILY LOAD (TMDL), WHICH IS ESTIMATED AT
  $744.90 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-24

  The Los Angeles River and tributaries Toxic Pollutant Total Maximum Daily
  Load (TMDL), adopted by the Regional Water Quality Control Board requires
  Los Angeles River watershed cities and agencies to monitor levels of Toxic
  Pollutants in the river and its tributaries. In July 2018, San Gabriel, along with
  other agencies, approved a Memorandum of Agreement with the Los Angeles
  Region Integrated Regional Water Management Joint Powers Authority
  (GWMA) to oversee a coordinated monitoring program. If entered in a three-
  year coordinated monitoring program, the annual cost for Fiscal Year 2023-24
  is $744.90 for Fiscal Year 2023-24, $748.12 for Fiscal Year 2024-25, and
  $765.68 for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023  5
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Memorandum of Agreement with the Los Angeles
  Gateway Region Integrated Regional Water Management Joint Powers
  Authority (GWMA) for a period of three years.

  H. AGREEMENT FOR PARKING CONSULTANT SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $19,800

  The City’s parking program consists of parking enforcement, citation
  management, and permit processing. To better manage this important
  program, staff proposes to enter into a Professional Services Agreement with
  an expert in municipal parking operations to develop a fully integrated
  parking program that will improve the experience for all involved. Both the
  Finance and Police Department have budgeted Parking Consulting Services
  for Parking Enforcement and Citation Management and for an automated
  parking permit system. The fiscal impact is $19,800 with $12,000 from the
  Police Department and $7,800 from the Finance Department.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a Professional Services Agreement with Dixon Resources Unlimited for
  parking consulting services. Their services would include the Request for
  Proposals, project management, procurement support services, and
  presentation to the City Manager and Council for parking enforcement,
  automated permit processing and citation management.

  I. AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $34,886.10 FOR PRINTING AND MAILING SERVICES FOR THE DISCOVER
  SAN GABRIEL PUBLICATION

  On April 18, 2023, Council authorized the professional services agreement
  with We the Creative to design a new publication, Discover San Gabriel. Staff
  released a request for proposals for printing and mailing services on August 9,
  2023 and received seven proposals. The current Fiscal Year 2023-24 general

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023  6
   fund budget includes a total of $98,804 within the non-departmental account,
  121-721-00-62-000, for the graphic design, printing and mailing of Discover
  San Gabriel. This budget is adequate to cover the annual graphic design cost
  of approximately $41,000, annual printing cost as proposed at $34,886.10 and
  annual mailing costs of approximately $20,000. Although the cost increases
  over the next several years the cost for the graphic design services decreases
  next fiscal year by approximately $9,500 ensuring the total project stays within
  budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the Professional
  Services Agreement with Advantage Mailing LLC to provide printing and
  mailing services for a term of three years and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. GENERAL FUND PRELIMINARY FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR ENDING JUNE 30, 2023

  The staff report presents the preliminary financial results for the City’s general
  fund for the Fiscal Year ending June 30, 2023. The presented financial results
  are unaudited and consist of forecast and estimates made by staff. Audited
  financial statements for the Fiscal Year ending June 30, 2023, will be published
  by December 31, 2023. There is no fiscal impact related to this staff report.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and file this report.

  B. FUNDING FOR THE SAN GABRIEL CHAMBER OF COMMERCE IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $23,000

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 5, 2023  7
   For many years, the City has supported the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce
  (Chamber) financially and through a variety of joint efforts that promote San
  Gabriel businesses. Though the City and Chamber continue to serve the
  business community, the City has not provided any funds to the Chamber as it
  did prior to 2020. Recently, the Chamber requested the City purchase a
  Presidential Circle Membership for $23,000. The timely request aligned with
  discussion of the City’s Fiscal Year 2023-2024 operating budget. This report
  examines the historical relationship between the City and the Chamber that
  culminates to the most recent request, includes other Cities’ contract amounts
  with their respective Chambers as points of reference, and presents several
  options for the City Council to consider in this matter.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  City Council Options:

  The following are options for the City Council regarding this matter:

  1. The City purchase a Presidential Circle Membership for $23,000. In addition
  to the membership, both parties – the City and the Chamber – enter into an
  Agreement that includes a ‘Scope of Work’ and a list of deliverables. Such
  potential agreement could be considered at a future City Council meeting
  and then provided to the Chamber for execution.
  2. The City purchase a Presidential Circle Membership for $23,000 (without an
  accompanying agreement).
  3. The City proceed with the existing relationship with the Chamber, which
  currently does no include any financial support, The City and the Chamber
  would process with respective efforts – both separate and joint – in
  supporting San Gabriel businesses.
  4. The Council may also consider other options (not listed above) as a result
  of discussion on this matter.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 5, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:32 P.M. on Tuesday, September 5, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Harrington.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward
  Macias,  Finance  Director  William  Kaholokula,
  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes,
  Police Chief Edward Elizalde, and Assistant City Clerk
  Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Special City Council Meeting of September 5, 2023:

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL -  ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION

  City Attorney Lemieux announced that the City Council gave unanimous direction

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  how to request meeting agendas.

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved .

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 6  September 5, 2023

  Mayor Harrington made the presentation and Council Member Menchaca received

  The following provided comments or spoke in favor of another pickleball court at

  The following spoke in opposition to another pickleball court at Smith Park: Christina

  Mary Garcia, resident, thanked the City for cleanup done near the freeway on Del Mar

I  Andrew, resident, commended Police Captain Riki Nakamura for a job well-done as

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

I  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  H. AGREEMENT FOR PARKING CONSULTANT SERVICES IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $19,800

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. GENERAL FUND PRELIMINARY FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE FISCAL VEAR
  ENDING JUNE 30, 2023

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Andrew, resident, questioned the Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB) liability
  status and received a response of a positive status change from Finance Director
  Kaholokula and City Manager Lazzaretto.

  Discussion included the greatly-improved reserves status; a request to separate
  out the line item for the payoff of the Public Works loan; kudos on the report and

I  the financial strides made; and desire for a new public-safety facility.

  B. FUNDING FOR THE SAN GABRIEL CHAMBER OF COMMERCE IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $23,000

  Economic Development Manager Caroline Velarde made the presentation .

  The following provided comments or spoke in opposition to funding the San
  Gabriel Chamber of Commerce: George Valdez; Carina Rivera, resident; Sean
  McMorris, resident; and Cheryl Cabot, resident.

  The following spoke in favor of the City purchasing a Presidential Circle
  membership with the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce: Gilda Moshir, Chamber
  Board Member; and Gary Wat, Chamber Board Member, resident.

  Discussion included confirmation that Mayor Harrington has no conflict of interest
  on this matter; disappointment that the Chamber's minutes were not included in
  the City staff report; concern about the resignation of six Chamber board members,

I  Chamber debt; the Executive Director's salary; the first-time Presidential Circle
  membership created just for the City, low Chamber membership; the logic of the
  City and the Chamber working together; higher costs paid by nearby cities to their
  Chambers than the amount proposed for San Gabriel; satisfaction of business
  owners with the San Gabriel Chamber; importance of a Chamber to businesses and
  residents; neighboring cities have service agreements with their Chambers;
  clarification that Vice Mayor Wu and Council Member Ding have no conflict of
  interest on this item as Chamber members; Chamber plans to increase membership
  to carry out the next fiscal year responsibly; benefits of Chamber membership;
  membership versus a contract; the Chamber's outstanding small-business loan;

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  September 5, 2023
   whether Chamber minutes are public record; past history of contracts between the
  City and the Chamber; preference for a service agreement; benefit of supporting
  the financial stability of the Chamber; the Chambers of nearby cities have various
  levels of membership; unethical release of Chamber records; having a loan equals
  opportunity not insolvency; the proposed $23,000 cost for membership is lower
  than surrounding cities; benefits to the City from Chamber membership; examples
  of nearby cities that don't have Chambers; Chamber Past-President Joanna
  Jimenez' concerns with the Chamber's financial status; Chamber membership drop
  during the COVI D pandemic and current membership of 170 businesses; four of

I  nine Chamber board members have businesses in San Gabriel; and open
  negotiations with the Chamber if a contract is considered .
